description: Retained public-log bytes for one controlled OMP frame workload, before and after the issue #686 log policy. Both runs use the same driver, the same batches and the same provider-free fixture; only the executable differs.

hosts.baseline: Darwin arm64 development host, release 1.1.0 executable
hosts.candidate: Linux x86_64 homelab runner, bend 2.0.25 with clang-19

batches.cumulative: 1000 message_update frames with a 51-character step, each carrying the whole accumulated message
batches.tool: 1000 tool_execution_update frames with a 51-character step, each carrying the whole accumulated partial result
batches.raw: 8 fixed lines that pin the classification of frames whose type field is unusual

interpretation: A `message_update` frame was already dropped before this change, so the `small` and `cumulative` batches retained the same bytes in both runs. The `tool` batch retains every frame in the baseline and one held frame in the candidate. The candidate's `retained_log_bytes` is larger than its per-batch figure because the turn writes the last held `tool_execution_update` when it ends: 52,812 bytes of partial result for the open call, plus the raw batch and the filter note. That write is the evidence an interrupted call would otherwise lose.
limits: The fixture starts no provider; the batches are frames the driver writes, so the numbers cover the coordinator's retention and not a provider's own behaviour.
The CPU figures the driver records come from different hosts and are not comparable; only the byte figures are.
One receiver process, one database and one log path per run; concurrent writers are covered by bend2/test/logs.py and not by this driver.
The workload is one 1000-frame batch per frame type, not a working day of coordination.
